title: Tool Contract Migration Checker
tagline: Find the saved tool calls that a proposed schema change would break.
summary: Help tool authors evolve a callable interface while existing agents still hold old argument shapes. Compare a documented subset of before-and-after schemas, generate counterexamples for required fields and narrowed values, and replay saved calls through both validators. Export a compatibility report and reviewable migration fixtures for CI.
youWillBuild: A schema compatibility CLI, breaking-call fixtures and a CI compatibility report.
skills: Load versioned tool contracts and saved calls
Export migration fixtures and a compatibility gate

prerequisites.title: JSON Schema basics (properties, required, types, enums)

stages.title: Load versioned tool contracts and saved calls
stages.summary: Validate basic schema structure, parse recorded argument payloads, and verify that saved calls conform to the original contract.
stages.doc:
Stage 1 of 4. Read the [project prerequisites](https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch/blob/9712e323fde8cb2ec933310ac619e920e8e31017/projects/tool-contract-migration-checker/README.md) before starting; this stage builds the foundation for schema comparison.

## What changes

When an AI tool contract evolves, we must parse both the old schema and the proposed schema into a normalized internal representation, and validate recorded historical agent invocations against those contracts.

The boundary for this stage is `load_contract`, `load_calls`, and `validate_call`.

## Work through one concrete case

A tool contract specifies required parameters, property types, and validation keywords like `enum`, `minimum`, and `maximum`.

```figure
pj-tool-contract-migration-checker-1
```

A valid call provides the required parameters matching their declared types. If a historical invocation omits a required property or violates a constraint, `validate_call` detects the mismatch and returns structured issue messages.

## Implement the contract

Implement `load_contract`, `load_calls`, and `validate_call` in your workspace `main.py`.

- `load_contract(raw)` verifies that `raw` is a dictionary with `type: "object"` and returns a normalized dictionary.
- `load_calls(raw)` takes a list of objects each containing an `arguments` dictionary.
- `validate_call(contract, args)` evaluates the call against declared properties, checking required fields, property types, bounds, and enum membership.

## Verify and inspect

From the repository root, initialize once:

```bash
python3 scripts/project_test.py tool-contract-migration-checker --init learning-artifacts/tool-contract-migration-checker
python3 scripts/project_test.py tool-contract-migration-checker --stage 1 --path learning-artifacts/tool-contract-migration-checker --strict
```

## References

[JSON Schema 2020-12 Validation](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation)

stages.title: Classify supported schema changes
stages.summary: Compare before and after schemas to categorize changes into compatible, breaking, and unresolved keywords.
stages.doc:
Stage 2 of 4. Read [Stage 1](https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch/blob/9712e323fde8cb2ec933310ac619e920e8e31017/projects/tool-contract-migration-checker/stages/01-load-contracts-and-calls/docs/en.md) before starting; this stage compares two loaded contracts.

## What changes

When modifying an AI agent's tool interface, not all changes have the same impact. Adding an optional argument allows existing callers to continue operating unmodified. In contrast, adding a required field, removing a field, tightening allowed bounds, or narrowing allowed enum variants immediately breaks deployed agents.

The boundary for this stage is `classify_changes`.

## Work through one concrete case

Consider evolving a database search tool:

```figure
pj-tool-contract-migration-checker-2
```

If version 2 introduces a required `auth_token` or restricts `max_results` from 100 to 50, all historical agent plans relying on the broader contract will be rejected.

## Implement the contract

Implement `classify_changes(old_contract, new_contract)` in your workspace `main.py`.

Categorize each detected change into:
- `breaking`: added required property, removed property, narrowed type, narrowed enum, tightened minimum/maximum/minLength/maxLength, or changed `additionalProperties` from `True` to `False`.
- `compatible`: added optional property, widened type, widened enum, relaxed bounds, or enabled `additionalProperties`.
- `unresolved`: a keyword outside the supported subset, such as `$ref`, `oneOf`, `pattern` or `format`, whose value differs between the two versions, or a changed nested `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties` or `items` inside a property. Annotations (`title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`) are ignored, and an unsupported keyword that did not change is not reported.

Each change object must include:
```python
{
    "type": "breaking" | "compatible" | "unresolved",
    "category": str,
    "property": str,
    "description": str
}
```

## Verify and inspect

```bash
python3 scripts/project_test.py tool-contract-migration-checker --stage 2 --path learning-artifacts/tool-contract-migration-checker --strict
```

## References

[Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/)

stages.title: Generate and replay breaking-call counterexamples
stages.summary: Synthesize minimal argument payloads that satisfy the old contract but fail the new contract, and replay saved calls through both validators.
stages.doc:
Stage 3 of 4. Read [Stage 2](https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch/blob/9712e323fde8cb2ec933310ac619e920e8e31017/projects/tool-contract-migration-checker/stages/02-classify-schema-changes/docs/en.md) before starting; this stage turns classified changes into concrete failing call fixtures.

## What changes

Static schema diffs show what changed in the abstract, but developers need concrete counterexamples: an exact payload that passed the old contract yet fails the new contract. Furthermore, running recorded production tool calls through both validators shows whether any actual historical usage is disrupted.

The boundary for this stage is `generate_counterexamples` and `replay_calls`.

## Work through one concrete case

When a new required field `session_id` is introduced:

```figure
pj-tool-contract-migration-checker-3
```

The synthesizer creates a minimal payload omitting `session_id` (satisfying the old contract) and verifies it fails the new contract with a `"missing required property: session_id"` error.

## Implement the contract

Implement `generate_counterexamples(old_contract, new_contract)` and `replay_calls(old_contract, new_contract, calls)` in your workspace `main.py`.

- `generate_counterexamples` tries to build one minimal payload for each breaking change: added required fields, removed properties, narrowed and introduced enums, narrowed types, tightened bounds, and closed schemas. It keeps a payload only after checking that it passes the old contract and fails the new one. When no candidate does, it leaves that change without a counterexample instead of emitting a wrong one.
- `replay_calls` partitions saved historical calls into:
  - `preserved`: valid under both old and new contracts.
  - `broken`: valid under the old contract but rejected by the new contract.
  - `already_invalid`: rejected by the old contract.
  - `breaking_rate`: `len(broken) / (len(preserved) + len(broken))` (or 0.0 if empty).

## Verify and inspect

```bash
python3 scripts/project_test.py tool-contract-migration-checker --stage 3 --path learning-artifacts/tool-contract-migration-checker --strict
```

## References

[Property-Based and Generative Testing](https://hypothesis.works/)

stages.title: Export migration fixtures and a compatibility gate
stages.summary: Produce a machine-readable compatibility report, export standalone test fixtures for migration tests, and implement a CI gate CLI.
stages.doc:
Stage 4 of 4. Read [Stage 3](https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch/blob/9712e323fde8cb2ec933310ac619e920e8e31017/projects/tool-contract-migration-checker/stages/03-generate-and-replay-counterexamples/docs/en.md) before starting; this stage integrates contract checking into a reusable CI gate.

## What changes

In modern AI agent deployments, schema changes must be validated automatically in continuous integration. This stage builds a comprehensive report generator, exports reproducible regression fixtures, and exposes a CLI gate that fails CI builds whenever breaking schema changes or replayed call failures are detected.

The boundary for this stage is `build_report`, `export_fixtures`, and the `cli.py` entrypoint.

## Work through one concrete case

A CI pull request proposes tightening tool arguments:

```figure
pj-tool-contract-migration-checker-4
```

Running `cli.py --old schema_v1.json --new schema_v2.json --strict` exits with status `1`, blocking the merge until the developer relaxes the contract to restore backwards compatibility.

## Implement the contract

Implement `build_report` and `export_fixtures` in your workspace `main.py`.

- `build_report(old_contract, new_contract, changes, counterexamples, replay_result)` produces a structured summary including schema version, tool name, compatibility status, and counts.
- `export_fixtures(output_path, counterexamples, broken_calls)` writes a clean JSON fixture file containing counterexamples and broken calls for regression testing.
- The supplied `cli.py` driver connects your cumulative functions to command-line flags.

## Verify and inspect

```bash
python3 scripts/project_test.py tool-contract-migration-checker --all --path learning-artifacts/tool-contract-migration-checker --strict
cd learning-artifacts/tool-contract-migration-checker
python3 cli.py --old samples/catalog_v1.json --new samples/catalog_v2.json --calls samples/saved_calls.json --output report.json
```

## References

[Continuous Integration and Schema Evolution](https://martinfowler.com/articles/evodb.html)
